perplexity.description:
Don't Prey For Me is the debut studio album by English rock band Little Angels, released in 1989 on the Polydor label. The album showcases a hard rock style characteristic of the late 1980s British rock scene, featuring energetic guitar-driven tracks with strong melodic hooks and the distinctive vocals of Toby Jepson. Produced by Owen Davies, the album contains 12 to 17 tracks depending on the edition, blending raw rock energy with polished production.

As the band's first full-length release, Don't Prey For Me established Little Angels' presence in the UK rock landscape, setting the stage for their subsequent albums, which achieved higher chart success, including Young Gods (1991) and Jam (1993), the latter reaching UK No. 1. While Don't Prey For Me did not attain major commercial breakthrough or high chart positions, it was important in building the band's early fan base and critical recognition for their energetic sound and songwriting.

Critically, the album is regarded as a solid hard rock debut that captures the band's raw potential and the late-80s rock vibe, though it did not reach the commercial heights of their later work. It remains a notable entry in Little Angels' discography for its role in defining their sound and launching their career under the Polydor label.
